Native OpenShot 1.4.3 settings sampler
====================================

settings-sampler.osp was saved and reopened by the actual OpenShot 1.4.3 GTK
application on 2026-11-20. It is NOT made from the modern compatibility stubs,
object.__new__, or a hand-written pickle encoder. author.py uses the installed
application's constructors, GTK main window, media importer, Project.Save, and
native open_project command. No application source was patched. The resulting
pickle bytes have not been edited. Only generated media and application data
are present; no customer assets or executable payloads are included.

Provenance
----------
Release: OpenShot 1.4.3 (final stable 1.x release), Debian package 1.4.3-1.
Source: official openshot.developers/ppa, archived Ubuntu Precise package:
https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/openshot.developers/ppa/ubuntu/pool/main/o/openshot/openshot_1.4.3-1_all.deb
Package SHA256:
513c9cec51856e77ec5bb3eae8b0ffc8ac6cb4ef5f92682adac31a7742be0049
settings-sampler.osp SHA256:
b49ef1b742768d2f7f430736e089296ef8006769045cfcd0c6811de97c74c1c7

Environment: isolated Ubuntu 12.04 Docker container, Python 2.7, python-gtk2
2.24.0-3, python-mlt3 0.7.6+git20120204-2, Xvfb, frei0r-plugins. The old PPA
.deb was installed with dpkg, with dependencies from Ubuntu's old-releases
archive. The host's OpenShot/system packages were not changed.

reference.mlt is the unedited XML generated by 1.4.3 for this project, before
saving. It supplies the historical renderer's interpretation for comparison;
modern OpenShot does not use MLT. Both files contain the original container
paths /work/sampler and /root/.openshot, not private user paths.

Contents (12 seconds)
---------------------
Project: HD 720p 25 fps, 1280x720, progressive, square pixels, 16:9; named
sequence, 30-second timeline workspace, 1-second ticks, three named markers.

Five tracks, listed from top to bottom:
  Hidden track: track video disabled; video clip with clip audio disabled.
  Muted track: track audio disabled; video clip with clip video disabled.
  Animated overlay:
    0-4s: red grid image; width 50->125%, height 75->110%, x -20->20%,
          y 10->-10%, alpha 0.6->1; no fill, left/top alignment, volume 80%;
          Brightness effect interpolates 0.75->1.25.
    4-8s: blue grid image, trimmed source 1-5s, rotation 12 degrees, distort;
          video fades 0.75/1.25s, audio fades 0.25/0.5s, volume 60%;
          Saturation effect 0.2 (frei0r.saturat0r).
    8-10s: test-pattern video, source 1-3s, clip audio muted, volume 65%.
    10-12s: test-pattern video, source 3-5s, clip video hidden, volume 20%.
    Reverse left-to-right wipe at 3.5s, length 1s, softness 0.15.
    Forward dissolve at 7.5s, length 0.5s, softness 0.7.
  Background: green grid image for 12s.
  Audio bed: generated 440 Hz tone, volume 35%, audio fades 0.5/1.5s.

Media: three generated 320x180 PNG grids, a generated mono PCM WAV, a generated
320x180 25 fps H.264/AAC test-pattern MP4, and the packaged 1.4.3 wipe SVG
(OpenShot's existing GPL asset). The media are deliberately small (under 0.4 MB).

What the modern tests cover
--------------------------
test_legacy_project.py reads the actual native bytes through the restricted
reader and verifies the profile, timeline, markers, shared media references,
track/clip mute and hide, animated geometry/opacity, effect parameters, fades,
and transition properties. It never loads historical application classes.

test_project_data.py tests the currently supported conversion in both
interactive and noninteractive modes with a window attached: media and clip
counts, track order, trims/positions, separate video/audio fade curves, volume,
transition direction/softness/resource, and modern Save As/reopen. Native 1.x
saves absolute paths; the test decodes the original file and relocates only
the inert media/transition records into a temporary copy. It does not rewrite
the fixture bytes or replace the real restricted parser with fabricated data.

Known conversion gaps: the modern converter currently ignores the legacy
project profile, timeline markers/zoom, animated scale/position/opacity,
rotation/alignment/fill/distort, track and clip mute/hide, and clip effects.
In particular the authored 25 fps profile becomes the user's default profile;
fade keyframes use that default's frame rate. The fixture preserves those
inputs for future conversion work. Passing tests do not claim full visual or
audio equivalence. Unsupported fields are checked at decoding, not asserted
to be discarded during conversion.

Reproduce with the real application
----------------------------------
From the repository root (Docker required):

  mkdir -p /tmp/openshot-143-build
  curl -fL https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/openshot.developers/ppa/ubuntu/pool/main/o/openshot/openshot_1.4.3-1_all.deb -o /tmp/openshot-143-build/openshot_1.4.3-1_all.deb
  docker build --network=host -t openshot-143-author -f src/tests/fixtures/legacy/openshot-1.4.3/Dockerfile /tmp/openshot-143-build

Make a writable COPY of this directory, then mount it at /work/sampler:

  cp -r src/tests/fixtures/legacy/openshot-1.4.3 /tmp/openshot-143-sampler
  docker run --rm --network=none -v /tmp/openshot-143-sampler:/work/sampler openshot-143-author

The application runs inside Xvfb and prints SAVED and REOPENED on success.
It writes settings-sampler.osp, reference.mlt, thumbnail/, and media/wipe.svg.
Real constructors generate new UUIDs, so regenerated bytes/hashes will differ.
The committed .osp is the original native Save output, not a normalized copy.
The authoring script is Python 2 and is not used by normal Python 3 unit tests.

For native reference rendering inside the same container (MLT 0.7.6):

  melt reference.mlt in=0 out=299 -consumer avformat:reference.mp4 vcodec=mpeg4 vb=1000000 acodec=aac ab=64000 strict=-2 s=640x360 threads=2 real_time=-1

For manual testing of the ORIGINAL pickle in modern OpenShot, make the saved
absolute media paths exist without modifying the bytes. For example, on a
disposable machine/container bind-mount this directory at /work/sampler, or
copy its media/ directory there, then open settings-sampler.osp. Ordinary
relocation through OpenShot's missing-file prompt is also possible. Do not
resave over the native original; save conversions to a separate JSON .osp.
